description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of problem types across different educational levels within the MathOdyssey benchmark dataset, with ten distinct categories shown as slices. The largest segment, colored dark blue, corresponds to "Algebra – Olympiad-level" at 21.19% (82 problems). Following this, the pink segment represents "Pre-Calculus – High School" at 14.21% (55 problems), and the light green segment indicates "Combinatorics – Olympiad-level" at 9.56% (37 problems). Other notable segments include "Algebra – High School" (light red, 17.83%, 69 problems), "Geometry – Olympiad-level" (orange, 6.46%, 25 problems), and "Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level" (magenta, 6.46%, 25 problems). Smaller segments include "Geometry – High School" (dark brown, 3.62%, 14 problems), "Calculus and Analysis – University-level" (grey, 6.20%, 24 problems), "Probability – University-level" (teal, 5.43%, 21 problems), "Statistics – University-level" (light blue, 4.39%, 17 problems), and "Olympiad-level" (light grey, 1.03%, 4 problems). Each slice is labeled with its category, percentage, and problem count, and the chart includes a legend-like key on the left for the Olympiad-level category. The segments are arranged in a clockwise descending order by size, starting from the largest at the top left.
